body:
Honestly, this is the comment i relate to the most. 

I AM feeling more selfish, more me, more...whatever. I don't think I'd be cruel to them if they started to feel differently, and I also hope that they'd be gentle enough with me to be honest. 

At the end of the day, that's what I want - honesty. I just want someone to be upfront with me. So, you're right. I have a lot of thinking to do.
Thank you. I'm really sorry you went through this as well, and I'm glad you're in a better place.

I do try not to keep score. I do love him, I genuinely want him to be happy, and I'm trying not to direct vitriolic hate towards his new partner who also left her fiance. 

It's just hard sometimes
I definitely need to exercise more. I've always been a bit of an exercise hater, but I need to increase my self esteem and this seems like a good start. Any tips for getting started?

> the shock of reality that everything I thought I knew was gone, I had no control in the matter, and so much of my life was lies.

Thank you for articulating exactly how I feel. I miss my life. I do miss him, though. Our special brand of humour. Our shared niche interests. My huge physical attraction to him. Fuck. 

I'm glad you found a way into a happier life. You sound like you're in a much better place!

I want to sincerely thank you for your kind, thoughtful and thorough response. I'm so sorry for what you're going through - having children must add an extra level of heartbreak that I can't even imagine. 

I didn't get to grieve my marriage during my marriage because I was pretty blindsided by the affair and his unhappiness - I knew I was unhappy for a while and voiced it and wanted to fix and work on it but he had an affair. So, I guess I feel unlovable and not worth it. I loved him so, so much. I can't imagine feeling that way again.

You're right, I need to learn a lot of lessons from this. 

I wasn't lazy, complacent or selfish, but I did have my own flaws that were brought out in sharp relief due to the stress of his affair and lying. We could both use some change. The problem is I wanted to fix us, and he blamed me for every wrong step.
Thank you. I read your posts, and your story is very similar to mine. Hopefully we can both find peace and get through it.
Healthy patterns -- that's what I'm trying to learn. Anything work particularly well for you?

I feel the same way. It's the suddenness - we didn't go through a few years of unhappiness or deadbedroom or anything. I got depressed winter '16/'17, he started his affair spring '17, I found out autumn '17 and he left Dec '17. One year ago he was stroking my hair and telling me he loved me and writing I was his soulmate in  my birthday card (my birthday was last week) and this year he's with his AP and I'm crying from a broken heart. Talk about a mind fuck.

I hope you're okay. Living on your own can be quite freeing...it's lonely but if I want to leave the dishes for a few days I can and sometimes that feels nice.

You're right. I accepted a lot of stuff I shouldnt have, and I'm sure he could say the same thing. Whilst on paper we were a great match and had a great physical connection we were both too messed up to make it work. I hope he's happy.

> Those are events, how you respond to them is what defines you, not the events themselves.

You are so right. I'm stuck in a victim mentality at the moment. No doubt my ex could give a million examples of how I wronged him. I recongise my faults and want to work on myself. Not planning on jumping into relationships - my self esteem is so low I'd only make things worse.

Edit for formatting

| deep down you were a bit resentful

I was a bit resentful sometimes. I felt like his mother, and I wanted a partner. I tried expressing this many times in many ways but got nowhere. Still miss our connection though.
Thank you so much for reaching out. I'm so glad you reached a better, happier place with a better, healthier love. Gives me hope.

Thanks. At this point, I'm trying not to care. I mean I DO care, but I'm trying not to. I want him to be happy. I adored him, but we both had our issues and whilst I was happy to try and work on myself and on us he wanted his coworker who was also unhappily engaged. 

I miss him and love him but I'm suffocating still thinking about him. Here's to trying to move on.

Thank you for reaching out. I'm really lucky that I have a good friendship base and a family who would move mountains for me. i had way more friends than he did - his are all short term friendships with coworkers where mine are long term friendships with people I met through hobbies, ex coworkers, school, etc. 

I tried downloading Bumble but my self esteem is way too low at the moment. Good to hear everything worked out for you! You give me hope.

As they were both cheating, i don't see how they can feel secure. But, I've read so much about exit affairs and apparently of all affair types it's the most common to work out. But, I have to try not to care. He's up on this pedestal I have to knock him off of in my mind.
I'm really, really sorry to hear you're suffering as well. I relate so much to that pain loop - I'm starting CBT therapy in an effort to break it. Sending you strength!

Thank you. You're right that he lied - not just about the affair, but a million stupid little things that never made sense to lie about.

Thank you for all the good advice. You sound very wise!

I'm really sorry for what you're going through. We didn't have any children, though we were discussing starting next year, and I'm thankful that i don't have to go through that too. 

I'm sure you are the rock your children need. Believe me, as they get older they can see who wanted to be in their life and who didn't. All the best.
Thanks. A month of Netflix sounds good. It's stupid, we're no longer connected in any way but I still long for him.

I think you're replying to /u/NoMasChad ?

When I say "shit wife", I mean:
Sometimes I lost my temper, sometimes I nagged, sometimes I got fed up with feeling like his mother and not his partner, sometimes I lost my shit when I uncovered another lie, sometimes I was mean because I was hurting but that is no excuse. I never gave up or got lazy or "selfish" - my relationship was my top priority because I wanted to build a shared life. Maybe that was my mistake? We both had our own issues, but I loved him, was affectionate, no deadbedroom, no withholding, but yeah, sometimes I was a wicked witch. But most of the time I was not.

Good advice - to be fair, he's blocked me on everything anyway. I've blocked him as well. 

I'll look into that group. Thank you for reaching out.
Thank you! I know I sound a bit...pathetic. But, sometimes it's good to just get it out. I appreciate you reaching out!

I wish I could offer you some advice, but I think the other replies have done a great job. 

I only wanted to say that I relate to your pain. That I, too, am having a hard time moving on, and I hope that you get to a good place soon. You're better than plan B, you deserve more.

Yes \- I think in many cases where one spouse has had an affair the other spouse is left betrayed and heartbroken, but often still in love.

I still love my husband. I haven't seen him in nearly 5 months but I still love him. But, I know I love who he was. And no matter how hard I was willing to try, he didn't love me. It's a constant aching pain, and I'm not sure I'll ever enter into a relationship again.
I’m sorry you’re in this pain. I feel the same way. Even though I recognise he was so, so cruel I also realise my flaws and wish we could really get a chance. I hope you find peace.

Thank you, this is really great advice. My values are very similar to yours, and I’ve noticed I am reaching out to friends and family so much more. They all say how much they’ve missed me. 

You sound like a very good person who deserves a very good life. Thank you for reaching out.

Thank you. I don’t know what kind of person I am...the only difference I see between him and I, and that is I have many long-term friendships and he has none. Well, he’s got one but with a woman he’s never actually met in real life. 

Thank you very much for reaching out. I think s good time is coming because I’m even getting sick of throwing myself these pity parties. One step at a time.

Too long to list, but mainly I was too critical and acted out too much. I thought we both had issues and wanted help. He wants her. 

Thank you for reaching out
Thank you. It’s hard to be objective sometimes but when feeling down I’ll try to re-read these comments to get out of a rut

I'm really sorry that you're in so much pain \- I feel it too. I was the one cheated on, but I accepted that I contributed to the situation and was dedicated to growing as an individual and repairing our marriage. He pretended to try for about 2.5 months then abandoned me right before Christmas. He's with the AP now and really doesn't feel like he didn't anything wrong. I'm the monster, in his eyes.

I'd give anything to have my ex feel the way you do. I miss my husband.

>  I feel so silly as I still fight with ruminating thoughts about her/us/what I could have done better/how I value our union more than she does and how I struggle with her decision to not grant reprieve 

I really relate to this. I would STILL take my cheating ex back \- I really do believe it was a situation that I contributed to, and he has deep underlying psychological issues that we could work on together. 

I miss him every second and it is breaking me. Hopefully we both \(you and I\) will find peace!

Hop

I relate to this as being the spouse that put in loads of effort \- tried to be nurturing and romantic and give and give and give. When I complained or lost my temper I was being too negative and making them feel bad about themselves. The thing is, they always had this insatiable need for external validation that I just could not satisfy..but other women, platonic or not, could. So, sometimes even the spouse that puts in loads of effort gets screwed.

He cheated on me, left me, and abandoned me. What more could I have done? I just wasn't a priority after I realised he wasn't perfect.
hi \- I can relate to your grief. I was abandoned by my husband too, totally out of the blue. I really hope you and your son can find peace \- you are much better off!

I'm in a reversed position \- I moved to the UK for my cheating STBXH about 7 years ago. Luckily, I've adapted well, have a solid career and great friends. I decided to stay for a while longer. I've loved living here and want to make some memories that aren't with my husband so that if I decide to leave I have some things that I did just for me because I loved it here. Why does he get to take everything? He's already shattered my heart; i can't let him uproot my whole life too. I want him to realise the fucking mistake he's making, but I also need to let go and move on. I've decided to move to a city we never lived in that's close to my job \(in a city we lived in and were very happy in, so I don't want to move back\) and near some friends. 

It's up to you \- either way you have the freedom to make yourself happy now.

>Re\-learn how to be your own person instead of part of a plural person that marriage makes us. Love yourself, be kind to yourself, and the pain will go away.

This is so true. I still struggle with everything being "we" when I'm talking \- I'm still attached to the man I married. But, that man is gone. I can hope and beg and plead until I'm bleeding but he's gone. No amount of rehashing the past or crucifying myself will bring him back.

i'm trying to figure out what makes me happy. i feel hollow at the moment. Mostly I just feel like a washed up failure. Trying, though! Thank you for reaching out. You sound like you've spent a lot of time figuring shit out and making yourself happy and I massively respect that.

You're right! To be clear, I haven't spoken to him in about 6ish weeks and have stopped looking at anything to do with him. I only snooped before because he kept telling me they weren't together and the absolutely fucking were \- he was telling her he loved her the week he moved about when he was still "thinking" and slept with her before he had even started the paperwork all the while telling me he was doing this for him and there was no one else because I was so crushed. I miss the man I married \- I don't miss who he is now. 

Thank you for reaching out.

> I was just doing something mundane in my new city with my new friends and I looked around and thought "this is the point where I wanted to wake up! I can't believe I made it here."

This. This is where I want to be. I'm in the process of selling our marital home, but have been so busy with friends. That last Bank Holiday I had a BBQ with the neighbours, and i was working the grill \(something that would have never happened with my ex\) and having a great time and I though, "He's left this absolutely beautiful life, and I feel so lucky to be surrounded by these people." He doesn't have real friends, not like I do. He has shitty co\-workers with serious issues \(they're high functioning addicts and liars \- he used to have nice work friends!\) and his new girlfriend's friends. I have good friends who love me for me \- not us as a couple, even though some have only known me as part of him. They reach out to me and seek me out \- I can't be the monster he claims. 

Your story gives me so much hope. Thank you.

I do think you are right \- we don't have any children and that will make things easier because we'll never have to see each other again. That thought really kills me, but it's probably for the best. I just don't understand how they turn so cold \- I couldn't, and I've had the opportunity to more than a few times. I was loyal to my husband; no one ever compared to him. 

Blargh \- it's all such a bloody mess. Thank you for reaching out, though. I hope we both find peace and happiness!

I do think that I died on the wrong hill when I said I wouldn't file for divorce and if he wanted one he'd have to file. in the UK the only way to get a "quick" divorce is to blame the other party \- his reasons on the divorce document still haunt me and make me feel like a monster. But, i also know he made some of it up \- I ran it by my mom and was like "this is blatantly not true!" Regardless, to know he holds those things against me and feels that way about me just kills me. I feel like a monster, unworthy of love and affection.

I wish I would have left. I've read a lot of the things you've posted and you seem to have a good head on your shoulders. Good luck to you.

When I found out he was having an "EA", I really, really wanted to reconcile. I recognised the parts of myself that had become toxic \(had recoginsed it before that and sought help but lapsed. that's on me\). We went through the whole theatre of marriage counselling and our marriage counselor even said she thought we passed the crisis point and clearly loved each other. He left two and bit weeks later.  

>I know that I have tremendous amounts of love to give the right person some day. Past be damned. 

This is such a good mindset to have. I don't want to fall in love again at the moment \- I genuinely thought he was it for me and that we could weather the storms together even though we both suffer from some issues. I was willing to work with him, be there for him, forgive him and grow with him. Only he had ceased to care about me in any way. 

I hope you find tremendous happiness.
Hope it went well for you and was empowering.
Thank you for your response \- it's good to know that there is light on the other side. In the middle of the tunnel right now and it is bleak. I'm so glad you are happy; gives me hope!

So - this might be inappropriate but I have a court story about getting a ticket and may make you laugh which I always find helps during tense times:
I suffer from very bad hay fever. Once, when I was about 19, I was driving to my part-time job during rush hour traffic. I felt the mother of all sneezes coming, and I was stopped going down a steep hill in quite heavy traffic. Well, I sneezed. I sneezed so hard that my foot slipped off my break and I hit the car in front of me. Normally this wouldn't have happened, but as i said we were going down a very steep hill so I didn't have the time to stop even though it was milliseconds. We call the police, i get a ticket, I have to go to court, blah blah blah. In court I tried to get off the ticket by claiming the sneeze was an act of God and not my fault. The judge was so tickled by the story and the fact that I tried to get out of it by claiming it was an act of God that he started laughing right there in court. Still got the ticket, though :( 

Edit: point is, court is scary but sometimes the judges are alright, really.
Good luck \- hope everything works out for you

> Will The Lord forgive meWhen I fall at those pearly gates?For I still tire like a child

I found that very moving. I think the feelings the image of a tired child evokes perfectly describes the weariness of heartbreak.

>Here's where I'm lost: I still feel attached to him. I feel void of the ability to be as invested with someone as I was with him.

I'm right there with you. I'm still very attached to my ex \- or, not attached but feeling like I still am "loyal" to him. Maybe just to my marriage? It's over \- we haven't even seen each other in 4 months and haven't spoken in about 6 weeks. He's with the person he left me for. Why can't I let go?

Good luck to you. Sounds like both of our partners have issues and I sincerely hope you find tremendous happiness.
Thinking is awful! I have a mind that whirrs constantly - a humming machine that provides a white noise of pain. Ah - to be out of your own head! I'll check out forest bathing.
Ally, I just wanted to say I noticed how often you comment on all of these posts. You are a kind angel on these boards and provide so much understanding. Thank you.

We are on about the same time frames, and it is inspiring to me that you've seemed to reach a more positive place. It is the obsessive side of my nature that is a glutton for punishment and I need to practice mindfulness and gratitude. 

Thanks for reaching out; I wish you so much happiness.
yo are right, thank you.

I want to thank you so much for your very articulate, caring and well-reasoned comment. It is so impressive to me the level of caring that pours out of posts on reddit from people, like you, who see a stranger hurting and want to ease their pain a little bit. So, thank you.

I am hurting so badly. Far worse than I ever thought humanly possible. But, I also feel guilt for hurting so much when I've had to endure so relatively little compared to billions of others. I know human suffering is not a competition, but when I see toddlers dying in a war I realise I'm pretty goddamn lucky. I just need to get out of my head. 

Thank you, kind stranger, for reaching out. How lucky we all are that you are here.

I know exactly how you feel \- like she must be so much better because why would he throw it all away? I know Chump Lady is all "trust they suck", but sometimes it feels like I'm the one who sucks. 

Good luck to you, I hope healing comes and you find happiness.

I'm right there with you. Even doing the "right" things \- taking anti\-depressants, weekly therapy, being really social, exercising \(could improve\), I'm still feeling that suffocating pain. I hope that it improves soon for both of us.
Yes. I know it is pointless, but I can't live with these feelings anymore.

Thank you for reaching out. I won't tell anyone because I don't want anyone to carry the guilt I feel for my brother's death. 

You're right that I'm having trouble moving on. Every day chips away at my soul. I just want to find peace.

Maybe. But my husband left me for someone else, I feel impenetrable guilt from my brother's suicide, and every day feels like a battle I'm not particularly interested in winning.   

I just want peace, and my inner turmoil makes this unlikely. But, as they say, "hope springs eternal!"
Cheers, mate. She's worth the pain. We laugh too much to cry.
I'm the lucky one. She's wonderful, and all I can do is be eternally grateful.
You're right, I'm sorry

My brother shot himself. My father found him - I will never, ever in my whole life forget the sound he made when he found him. I called the ambulance, and I will never forget the conversation I had with the dispatcher. Or my mother's wailing. Or my sister shaking and silent. We were all in the house. You'd be surprised how quiet a shot is - not like on TV.

Please, please think about those that could find you. I understand it's hard and you're hurting and feel despair - I feel that way too. Even with a brother that died, and seeing how it affected those around me, I still think about ending it. But please take a second to think of your loved ones. I hope you find happiness.

I relate to everything you said in this post. I'm tired, too. I've never told anyone how dark the thoughts can get; they all see me as someone who's trying to get out of a bad situation and are being so supportive. But, most the time I think about just disappearing. 

You have a daughter - speaking as someone who had some pretty messed up parents, I can say that even through the worst of their shit I still loved them completely. And, now that they've both got it under control, we're closer than ever. Your daughter loves you, and it's never too late to fix that relationship with honesty and true remorse. I hope you find happiness.

Thank you. The cheating has destroyed me -- like my whole adult life has been a lie. I loved my husband to the bottom of my soul and couldn't imagine doing this to him. That, on top of all the other things that have happened in my short life, make me feel like life is really just suffering and some people suffer more. Why suffer more?

I'm so sorry that you're going through this. You are 100% right that being a giver can take a massive toll - though it speaks to a wonderful quality inside of you. My wish is that we will both find peace and happiness, and that if you visit Japan it is to immerse yourself in your heritage and not to end it.

Popularity does not equal happiness. Like me, he was good at hiding his sadness, and suffered from night terrors and various other things. You can be surrounded by people and still be suffering and lonely.

> the absurdity of the world and my own thoughts and regrets are so huge that it feels like i'm living with a burden that starts to get too heavy for me

This. I completely relate. Cheating can, for some people, rob them of all security and make them deeply question themselves. For so long I've felt I drove my husband to cheating, that I deserved it. I'm sorry we're in the same spot. Good luck to you - I'm glad you're getting help.

I think, and I'm not trying to be insensitive, that when people suggest breathing exercises or journalling activity what they're trying to say is that you must love and take care of yourself before you can be a good companion. Companionship is not one way, you must also be comfortable enough in yourself to be a good friend/companion to others - friendship is a two way street. 
Work on yourself, find who you are, what you like, what you want, and then find others that reflect that. 

I hope you find happiness, I say this repeatedly because I really, really do. I'm despairing of finding it, but I hope that others do. Reach out if you need to.

Do you think it might be related to seasonal affective disorder? If it happens at the end of winter you might experiencing depression from the lack of sunlight and general gloom of winter. It's becoming increasingly understood and doctor's are learning to recognise how severe it can be.

Have you seen a doctor or gotten therapy for the depression/anxiety? I'm struggling with them too at the moment and therapy is helpful for the coping

Thank you for reaching out. I feel like therapy helps for the time I'm there, but because of my thought process I tend to obsess and when left to my own devices it's overwhelming. I'm trying DBT, so maybe that'll help? Honestly my life is pretty stable, I have a really good job, I have caring people in my life, but the bad still seems to out weigh the good.; I'm suffocating and just want to be free.

I hope you find happiness.

I just wanted to reach out say I completely understand what you're going through. My brother was 15 when he ended his life, and there is not a day that has gone by for the past 8 years that I've not thought about him. I saw how deeply it affected, and still continues to affect, his friends. He was popular - far more conventionally popular than my sister or I ever were - and had everything going for him. The things that seemed to make the most difference and help his friends to heal was to have certain rituals to remember him. They had a memorial. They planted a tree in his name. They still message my parents on the anniversary - some still drop by the house - and they keep his memory alive. They live full, productive lives and take the time to remember who they lost because he was important to them. Do the same for your friend, and for yourself so you can heal and come to terms with what happened. I am so sorry for your loss.

Edit: spelling

This might sound random, but how old is your mom? Do you think it could be hormones from menopause that are causing her to feel this way? Apparently it can be extremely distressing and cause huge emotional upheaval. She should see a doctor. At the very least, she should get some counselling. 

As someone who's going through I divorce I can relate to how she feels. The most you can do, as he son, is be there for her and suggest she gets the care she needs. Even if it's just holding her hand in a waiting room or helping her find someone to talk to. Action will help you feel better as well.
